content:
maria: heads-up — customer purpleai reported a sudden embeddings throughput collapse on /v1/embeddings yesterday after the runtime deploy. They say vectors/sec dropped ~5x while token throughput (for our text-gen routes) stayed flat. raising here to crowdsource quick repro and mitigation. @jon @leo :wave:

jon: saw the alert. any error spikes in logs or 429s?

maria: no 429s, just long tail latency on the embeddings route. customer provided their perf numbers: used to be ~18k vectors/s, now ~3.4k. they batch 64 per request, 512-d model.

leo: hmm. batching reduction or queueing change could do that. what does GPU look like?

maria: customer snapshots attached in support ticket — pasted key metrics below:```
queue_depth: 120
avg_batch_size: 42
vectors_per_sec: 3400
tokens_per_sec (text-gen overall): 19000
gpu_util_percent: 94
gpu_mem_free_mb: 1024
kernel_busy_pct: 63
kv_cache_hits: high
```

maria: interestingly kernel_busy_pct ~63 while gpu_util high. suggests memory stalls or host-side queue bottleneck.

jon: can you share the exact model variant and runtime config? quantized? tiled kernels?

maria: model: open-embed-512-v2, quant: q4_0, runtime: r4.4, batching: auto (max_batch_tokens=16384), prefix_cache=enabled

leo: prefix_cache=enabled + quantized model + big batches = potential KV cache thrashing. If KV shards are being reallocated per request, we get host-side locking and queue pileup. Also if batches are smaller due to client behaviour, vectors/sec drops even if tokens/sec for gen stays fine.

support: customer reported they didn't change client code. they do have a nightly job that pins worker counts — might coincide with deploy.

maria: repro attempt on staging: I replayed similar traffic shape (constant ~250 rps with 64-item payloads). Locally I saw avg_batch_size become 24 and queue_depth rise to 80. When I disabled prefix_cache, avg_batch_size jumped back to 58 and vectors/sec recovered to ~16k.

jon: good repro. that implicates prefix_cache path. Any changes in the last deploy touching KV cache shard placement or gc?

leo: I rolled a change last week that adjusted the KV shard eviction heuristic (PR #4432) — it added a small mutex during cold-shard attach to avoid races. Could that be adding latency per request and preventing batching coalescing?

jon: if per-request latencies increase by ~5ms and bursts are tight, batching windows close earlier and you get smaller batches. smaller batches -> lower vectors/sec.

maria: I captured request logs and included per-request timings (timestamps truncated):```
[req_1001] enqueue_wait=2ms attach_kv=8ms dispatch=1ms exec=3ms
[req_1002] enqueue_wait=6ms attach_kv=9ms dispatch=1ms exec=3ms
[req_1003] enqueue_wait=0ms attach_kv=7ms dispatch=1ms exec=3ms
```

maria: attach_kv is showing 7–9ms on many requests. previously it was ~1ms.

leo: that aligns with the mutex hypothesis. need to verify PR #4432 change log. If we added synchronous io during attach, that kills the batching window.

jon: for a short-term mitigation we can: 1) disable the new eviction mutex flag, 2) disable prefix_cache for affected customers, or 3) temporarily increase batching window in runtime config (max_batch_delay_ms). Which is fastest?

maria: support already offered to flip prefix_cache for the customer — they're ok with a short blackout of cache. I prefer increase max_batch_delay_ms as non-invasive (but might increase latency P99).

leo: change to max_batch_delay_ms = 12ms (from 5ms) could allow batches to re-coalesce. That should be config-only and quick. Also add a rollback of PR #4432 to staging for validation.

support: customer prefers config change first. request ticket updated with suggested change.

jon: I'll push a runtime config tweak to the customer's pool: set max_batch_delay_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=32768 (double tokens) to help batch growth. Will monitor.

infra-sre-bot: deploy-notice: runtime-config-update applied to pool purpleai-embed-pool at 2026-03-14T21:32:00Z by jon.

maria: after config change customer reports vectors/sec climbed from 3.4k -> 14.7k in 10 minutes. queue_depth dropped to ~18.

leo: great. still want to root cause the new mutex. jon — can you open a revert PR for #4432 so we can test without the change and then craft a non-blocking attach path?

jon: will do. opening PR: https://git.redwood/r/infra/4432-revert-attach-mutex. I'll run a canary in staging.

maria: notes for postmortem / follow-up: - correlate KV attach latency distribution with batch sizes over last 72h - add telemetry for per-request attach_kv timings - consider async attach path or optimistic attach to avoid blocking batching thread - add test sim to infra CI that simulates high attach contention and measures batching windows

support: customer is happy with interim fix and asked for postmortem once we have action items. closing current support ticket after follow-up. :+1:

leo: assigning myself to the follow-up items. thanks everyone. :rocket:
